faqPage.title: How does e-tendering work? And other questions
faqPage.lead: Straight answers on online tenders, fees, building permits and supervision.
faqPage.searchPlaceholder: Type a word, e.g. permit or commission
faqPage.resultsCount: {count, plural, =0 {No results} one {# question} other {# questions}}
faqPage.empty: No question matches your search. Ask us directly and we'll answer.
faqPage.stillBody: Ask an engineer directly — no commitment.
faqPage.commissionTbd: The rate is agreed on award.

q1.a: Once the design is approved and the building permit issued, we publish your project on the platform with drawings, specifications and the BOQ. Registered contractors submit bids online until the announced closing date. We then open the bids, analyse them line by line, show you a clear comparison and evaluate the qualified companies with you present before the award.

q2.q: Is the service really free for the owner?
q2.a: Yes. The owner pays the platform nothing for design, tendering, bid evaluation, contract drafting or supervision. These services are covered by a commission paid by the winning contractor on award.

q3.q: How does the platform make money?
q3.a: The platform charges a commission to the winning contractor on award only; the owner pays nothing. {commission} Contractors know about the commission before they submit a bid.

q4.q: What do I need to start?
q4.a: Your plot plan, the title deed and, if your project is loan-funded, your approved Housing or QDB loan. If your documents aren't complete yet, start with the project brief and we'll tell you what's missing.

q5.q: Do you help me get a housing loan?
q5.a: No, we do not process loan applications. We work with the loan already approved by the Housing Department or QDB, and we prepare your design and technical documents to match the loan amount.

q6.q: How long does the design stage take?
q6.a: It depends on the size of the project, how quickly you approve drawings and how long the authorities take to respond. We give you a written timeline after the first meeting and tell you immediately if it changes.

q7.q: Who obtains the building permit from the Municipality?
q7.a: We do. We handle the building permit with the Municipality and the related approvals from Kahramaa and Civil Defence as part of our free owner services. We only need your documents and signatures.

q8.a: After opening the bids we analyse prices line by line, then evaluate the qualified companies on price, experience, capacity and schedule commitment, and review the results with you present. We recommend on published criteria; the final decision is yours.

q9.q: Can I invite a contractor I know to bid?
q9.a: Yes, provided they register on the platform and bid on the same documents and by the same deadline as everyone else, so the competition stays fair.

q10.q: What if the contractor breaches the contract?
q10.a: The contract we draft sets fixed durations, payments tied to progress and delay penalties. The supervising engineer records and documents any breach and notifies the contractor formally. We mediate to settle it amicably; if that fails, your rights remain protected under the contract.

q11.q: How do contractors and suppliers register?
q11.a: On the sign-up page, choose "Contractor" or "Supplier", enter your company and commercial registration details, then your contact details, then create a password. Once your details are reviewed, you'll receive tenders that match your classification or product categories.

q12.q: Do you supervise construction until handover?
q12.a: Yes. Our engineers follow the site through every stage of construction, check completed works before payments are approved and send you regular reports until handover.

f1.q: Can I build with a QDB loan?
f1.a: Yes. We work with loans approved by the Housing Department or QDB, and with self-funded projects. We do not handle the loan application itself.

f2.q: How much does it cost to build a villa in Qatar?
f2.a: Cost depends on area, floors, specifications and finishes. We prepare an estimate based on your design and BOQ before tendering, and the bids then reveal the real market price.

f3.q: Do I have to accept the lowest bid?
f3.a: No. We evaluate bids on price, experience, capacity and schedule, and the lowest price can be unrealistic. We show you why with numbers; the decision is yours.
